note: Complete public scientific-checker bank. Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set.

checkers.alarm: `theta_rad < x*(1 - C*eps)` or `theta_rad > x/sqrt(1-x^2) * (1 + C*eps)`; the slack is a few ulps of `theta` in the working precision of radius, distance and theta (float32 inputs give float32 slack) (arcsin plus two unit conversions through arcsec)
checkers.invariant: with `x = R/D`, the angular radius `theta` of a sphere seen from distance `D` satisfies `x <= theta <= x/sqrt(1-x^2)` (arc vs chord vs tangent)
checkers.precondition: `0 < R/D < 1` for the physical radius `R` and distance `D` (any finite quantities)
checkers.rationale: `sin(theta) = R/D` is the definition of the Sun's semi-diameter and every disk-limb test downstream relies on it.

checkers.alarm: `r` outside that interval
checkers.invariant: the distance lies between perihelion and aphelion of Earth's orbit, `0.9825 AU <= r <= 1.0175 AU` (`a(1-e)`..`a(1+e)` with `e = 0.0167`, `a = 1 AU`, margin 4e-4 AU for planetary perturbations and the Earth-Moon wobble)
checkers.rationale: a unit or ephemeris-body slip produces distances outside any Keplerian envelope.

checkers.alarm: relative difference `> 1e-11` (both are float64 chains of about 10 operations on 1.5e11 m, `C*eps` = 1.4e-14, margin 700x)
checkers.invariant: the Sun-Earth distance from barycentric positions equals the radial coordinate of `get_earth` (two independent paths: vector difference vs frame transformation)
checkers.rationale: two public APIs report the same physical quantity.

checkers.alarm: `|B0 - arcsin(p . e)| > 1e-11 rad` (B0 < 0.13 rad, so arcsin is well conditioned; both paths are float64 with about 30 operations)
checkers.invariant: `sin(B0) = p . e`, where `p` is the unit vector of the Sun's north pole in ICRS (constants `alpha_0`, `delta_0`) and `e` is the unit Sun->Earth vector from barycentric positions (no frame transformation involved)
checkers.rationale: B0 is by definition the heliographic latitude of the sub-Earth point, the angle between the rotation axis and the Sun-Earth line.
checkers.scientific_quantity: heliographic latitude of the sub-Earth point

checkers.alarm: `|true - mean| > 10.5 arcsec`, with `mean` from `mean_obliquity_of_ecliptic`
checkers.invariant: true minus mean obliquity is the nutation in obliquity, whose amplitude is 9.2 arcsec for the 18.6-year term and at most 10.5 arcsec in total
checkers.rationale: a wrong angle unit or a nutation term applied twice changes every apparent coordinate.

checkers.alarm: wrapped `|apparent - true| > 42 arcsec`
checkers.invariant: the difference of the Sun's apparent longitude (true equinox of date, aberrated) and true longitude (mean equinox of date, geometric) is the sum of the annual aberration (20.5 arcsec x 1 AU/r, at most 21.2) and the nutation in longitude (at most 19.5 arcsec including the 1.3 arcsec semiannual term), so at most 42 arcsec in magnitude (revised from 40, see revision log)
checkers.observation_point: return of `apparent_longitude`; the checker re-calls `true_longitude` at the same time
checkers.rationale: catches precession/equinox mismatches between the two definitions (X: the re-call is the identical time object).
checkers.scientific_quantity: apparent ecliptic longitude of the Sun

checkers.alarm: angular difference `> 1e-3 arcsec` (both chains use IAU 2006/2000A; rounding is below 1e-9 arcsec, the slack covers model-level differences far below any use)
checkers.invariant: the Sun's right ascension/declination referred to the true equinox of date equals its coordinates in astropy's `TETE` frame obtained from HCRS (an independent transformation chain)
checkers.rationale: cross-method consistency of a published solar ephemeris quantity.
checkers.scientific_quantity: apparent equatorial position of the Sun

checkers.alarm: wrapped `|lon| > 1e-9 deg` (rounding of the HGS rotation is about 1e-14 deg)
checkers.invariant: in Heliographic Stonyhurst the Sun-Earth line projects onto zero longitude, so the longitude of the Earth is 0
checkers.rationale: the definition of the Stonyhurst frame must hold for the ephemeris path that feeds it.

checkers.alarm: `|ltt - |r_body(emitted) - r_obs|/c| > 1e-7 s` (the loop stops when successive estimates differ by 1e-8 s and the map is a contraction with rate `v/c ~ 1e-4`)
checkers.invariant: the final light travel time equals the distance between the observer and the body at the emission time, divided by `c`
checkers.precondition: an observer is supplied, finite positions
checkers.rationale: convergence of an iterative scientific algorithm at its end state.

checkers.alarm: absolute fraction difference `> 2e-3`
checkers.invariant: the obscured fraction of the spherical-cap overlap equals the planar circle-lens-area fraction to within the curvature correction `O(theta^2)` (about 1e-4)
checkers.observation_point: before the return of `eclipse_amount`, from its `s`, `m`, `d` and `fraction`
checkers.precondition: Sun and Moon angular radii and separation all `< 0.02 rad`
checkers.rationale: independent geometric model of the same physical quantity.

checkers.invariant: the rotation number is monotonic in time and advances at `(Omega_sid - Omega_earth)/360 deg` per day with `Omega_earth` between 0.9525 and 1.0187 deg/day, i.e. 13.16-13.23 deg/day
checkers.observation_point: return of `carrington_rotation_number`; the checker re-calls it at `t + 1 day` (exact two-double addition, X ok)
checkers.rationale: wrap-adjustment mistakes shift the integer part by one rotation.

checkers.invariant: `carrington_rotation_number(carrington_rotation_time(c)) = c` to the documented 0.11 s
checkers.rationale: documented accuracy of a published conversion.

checkers.alarm: relative difference of `P_syn` `> 1e-4` (Julian vs sidereal year changes it by 1.3e-6)
checkers.invariant: the mean synodic period and the sidereal rotation rate satisfy `1/P_syn = Omega_sid/360 deg - 1/P_orbit` with the sidereal year `P_orbit = 365.256363 d`
checkers.rationale: physical-constant consistency against an accepted value.

checkers.alarm: wrapped longitude difference `> 1e-9 deg`
checkers.invariant: the Sun-disk centre seen from Earth (helioprojective `(0,0)`) lies at Carrington longitude `L0` (via HPC -> HCC -> HGS -> HGC; independent of the formula in `L0`)
checkers.rationale: the definition of `L0`, exercised through the frame graph (re-entrancy guarded).
checkers.scientific_quantity: Carrington longitude of the disk centre

checkers.alarm: wrapped difference `> C*eps*max((|A|+|B|+|C|)*|dt|, 360 deg)`
checkers.invariant: rotation at `-lat` equals rotation at `+lat` (the rate depends on `sin^2`)
checkers.rationale: the solar rotation profile is north-south symmetric.

checkers.alarm: rate at the higher latitude exceeds the lower by `> 1e-10 deg/day`
checkers.invariant: the one-day rotation rate is non-increasing in `|lat|`
checkers.observation_point: return of `differential_rotation`; re-call with `|lat|+5 deg` (capped at 90), duration 1 day
checkers.rationale: the equator rotates fastest for every published profile.

checkers.alarm: wrapped difference `> C*eps*max((|A|+|B|+|C|)*|dt|, 360 deg)` in degrees
checkers.invariant: `rot(dt) = 2 rot(dt/2)` modulo 360 deg
checkers.rationale: a constant angular velocity at fixed latitude.

checkers.alarm: relative deviation from `sunpy.sun.constants.sidereal_rotation_rate` `> 0.05` (published equatorial rates span 14.1-14.7 deg/day)
checkers.invariant: the equatorial one-day rotation of any model is within 5 percent of the sidereal rate `14.1844 deg/day`
checkers.observation_point: return of `differential_rotation`; re-call at latitude 0 and duration 1 day, sidereal
checkers.rationale: unit-conversion check of the model coefficients against the authoritative constant.

checkers.alarm: wrapped difference from the expected shift `> 1e-4 * 0.9856 deg/d * |dt| + C*eps*max(scale, 360 deg)`
checkers.invariant: sidereal minus synodic rotation equals `360 deg / 365.256363 d` times the elapsed time (mod 360)
checkers.observation_point: return of `differential_rotation`; re-call with the other `frame_time`
checkers.rationale: hard-coded constant checked against the orbital period.

checkers.alarm: relative deviation `> 0.10`
checkers.invariant: the one-day rate agrees with the mean of the other two differential models within 10 percent (Beck 2000 compares them at the few-percent level)
checkers.observation_point: return of `differential_rotation`; re-calls with the other models
checkers.rationale: cross-model consistency.

checkers.alarm: HGS Cartesian difference `> 1e-3 m + 1e-12 L + 64 eps_len L`, plus `64 eps_ang |p|` when the observer longitude/latitude are lower precision than float64; `L` = the largest of the point distances and the two observer distances, `|p|` the Sun-centred point radius, `eps_len` the largest epsilon among the observer radii and coordinate components, `eps_ang` that of the observer lon/lat
checkers.invariant: after `Helioprojective -> Helioprojective` with a different observer, both coordinates are the same Sun-centred point (compare in HGS)
checkers.precondition: same `obstime` for both frames, observers defined
checkers.rationale: a physical location does not depend on who observes it.

checkers.alarm: relative difference `> 1e-8` of `sin(theta)` (position evaluated in float64)
checkers.invariant: `sin(theta) = (D/r) sin(alpha)`, where `alpha` is the angle at the observer between the disk centre and the point (triangle observer-Sun centre-point)
checkers.precondition: a 3-D coordinate with observer, radius `r > 0`, point not on the Sun-observer line
checkers.rationale: relates the limb-darkening angle `mu` to the observed disk position.

checkers.alarm: any point's angular distance (via `atan2` of the HPC Cartesian vector, no cancellation) differs by `> max(1e-9, C*eps_in) theta + C*eps`, `eps_in` the largest unit round-off of observer radius and `rsun`
checkers.invariant: every limb point seen from the observer has angular distance `arcsin(rsun/D)` from the disk centre
checkers.rationale: ties the limb construction to the angular-radius law.

checkers.alarm: any angle error `> 64 eps / sin(Theta)`, `eps` the largest floating epsilon among the start, end and centre coordinates
checkers.invariant: the point at parameter `p` makes angle `p*Theta` with the start vector and `(1-p)*Theta` with the end vector (angles measured from the arc centre), independent of radius
checkers.rationale: a great-circle path is a constant-speed geodesic.

checkers.alarm: `| |d u - C| - R | > 1e-9 R + C*eps*(|C| + |C|^2/R) + C*eps_in*(R + |C|)` (`eps_in` the largest unit round-off of centre, distance, radius) or `d < C.u - tol`
checkers.invariant: the promoted point `d u` is at distance `R` from the sphere centre and `d >= C.u` (the far intersection)
checkers.rationale: the defining geometry of the screen assumption.

checkers.alarm: for an element with a positive returned distance, residual `|delta/distance| > 1e-9` and exactly one genuine root (residual changes sign continuously, a root and not a pole) in 0.8-1.25 x the returned distance on 0.05 % steps, i.e. a nearby root that the local solve failed to reach; elements with no nearby root or several nearby roots (ill-posed fixed point) are not alarmed
checkers.invariant: at the returned distance the 3D->2D->3D shift is below the solver tolerance (documented 1e-11, accepted 1e-9)
checkers.rationale: convergence of the numerical solve at its end state.

checkers.alarm: `|dTx|,|dTy|` `> 1e-6 arcsec` plus a round-off allowance (`64 eps` relative to the angular offset and to `L/d`, `eps` the largest floating epsilon among the input components and observer radii; and `64 eps_o |p|/d` for observer lon/lat of epsilon `eps_o`, `|p|` the heliocentric radius of the point), or `|d distance| > 1e-12 D` plus `64 eps L` and `64 eps_o |p|`
checkers.invariant: rotating to a new observer/time and back to the original observer/time recovers the 3-D input
checkers.observation_point: return of `solar_rotate_coordinate`; the checker rotates back
checkers.precondition: coordinate with an HGS observer at its own `obstime`, on-disk (finite HGS), `observer` supplied
checkers.rationale: differential rotation changes longitude as a function of latitude only. N: blind to a global sign error, hence DRC-002.

checkers.alarm: wrapped change of the longitude of the HCRS Cartesian vector in the de-tilted frame (axis = solar north) differs from `drot` by `> 1e-8 deg + max(1e3 eps64, 64 eps_in)/cos(lat)` (`eps_in` the largest epsilon among the coordinate components and observer angles)
checkers.invariant: about the Sun's rotation axis, in an inertial (ICRS-oriented, Sun-centred) frame, a point's longitude advances by `differential_rotation(dt, lat)`
checkers.rationale: fixes the direction the reversibility law cannot see.

checkers.alarm: any corner moves by `> 1e-6` old pixel scales
checkers.invariant: the world coordinates of the four outer corners of the pixel grid (edges at `-0.5` and `n-0.5`) are unchanged by `resample`
checkers.rationale: resampling changes sampling, not the sky covered.

checkers.alarm: any corner differs by `> 1e-6` old pixel scales
checkers.invariant: the outer corners of the binned grid coincide with the old pixel-edge corners at `offset - 0.5 + dims*(edge + 0.5)`
checkers.rationale: binning keeps the sky area of the kept pixels.

checkers.alarm: output beyond the range by `> C*eps*max|x|`
checkers.invariant: output values lie within `[min, max]` of the input (maximum principle)
checkers.precondition: method `nearest` or `linear`, every new sample coordinate inside the old node range (no extrapolation), finite samples used
checkers.rationale: linear interpolation is a convex combination.

checkers.alarm: centre moves by `> 1e-6` old pixel scales plus `64 eps d`, `d` the pixel distance of the reference pixel from the array centre and `eps` the epsilon of the rotation matrix dtype
checkers.invariant: the array-centre pixel has the same world coordinate before and after `rotate` (padding and cropping are symmetric)
checkers.rationale: rotation about the centre must not shift the image.

checkers.alarm: non-integer offset `> 1e-6 + C*eps*180 deg / (absolute pixel scale in deg)` (world-to-pixel round-trip conditioning), scale change `> 1e-12` relative, or data mismatch
checkers.invariant: the submap's pixel `(0,0)` corresponds to an integer pixel `(x0,y0)` of the parent, the scale is unchanged, and the data equal `parent[y0:y0+ny, x0:x0+nx]`
checkers.rationale: cropping must not resample.

checkers.alarm: zero or more than one true
checkers.invariant: exactly one of `is_all_on_disk`, `is_all_off_disk`, `contains_limb` is true
checkers.rationale: the three classes are the possible relations between a rectangle and a disk.

checkers.alarm: result true but some pixel centre is off disk
checkers.invariant: when the edge test says all on disk, every pixel centre is on the disk (convexity)
checkers.precondition: map with at most 262144 pixels, field of view `<= 5 deg`
checkers.rationale: shortcut vs exhaustive cross-check.

checkers.alarm: result true but some pixel centre is on disk
checkers.invariant: when the edge test says all off disk, no pixel centre is on the disk
checkers.precondition: as MAP-007, and disk angular radius `>= 2` pixel steps, a step being the longest lattice vector of the full pixel-to-sky linear map (`PC` scaled by `CDELT`)
checkers.rationale: shortcut vs exhaustive cross-check.

checkers.invariant: resampling the ramp `a i + b j + c` (fixed float64, independent of the user data) returns the ramp evaluated at the physical sample positions `(i + o) s - o`
checkers.observation_point: return of `image.resample.resample`; re-run on the ramp
checkers.rationale: coordinate mapping check with a data-independent probe.

checkers.alarm: any differs by `> 1e-12` relative (time: beyond that resolution)
checkers.invariant: converting a frame to a WCS and back recovers frame class, `obstime` (to the resolution of the written time string: 1 ms or the frame time's `precision`, whichever is coarser), `rsun` and observer lon/lat/radius
checkers.precondition: Sun-fixed frame with an HGS/HGC observer frame
checkers.rationale: serialization must be lossless.

checkers.alarm: coordinate error `> 1e-9 + C eps 360 deg / scale` pixels, or step differs by `> 1e-9 + x^2/2 + C eps 360 deg / |scale|` relative (`x` = the step in radians; a zenithal pixel step of plane size `x` spans `atan(x)`; the last term is the rounding of two O(360 deg) coordinates differenced over one step)
checkers.invariant: evaluating the header's WCS at the zero-based reference pixel gives the input coordinate, and one pixel along an axis moves the coordinate by the requested scale
checkers.precondition: coordinate frame with lon/lat, `rotation_matrix` not given
checkers.rationale: FITS 1-based vs 0-based pixel conventions and units.
